verdict.wrong_value: Positions holding the old fill_value were relabelled rather than stored, so data values were lost/altered after astype; NaN gaps were mishandled (observed behaviour not recorded).
verdict.rationale: The PR fixes SparseArray/DataFrame.astype when the target SparseDtype requests a different fill_value or subtype. Tests assert values survive, NaN gaps remain NaN and block integer subtypes via IntCastingNaNError, and no float64 widening or index-kind loss occurs. This is numeric value and special-value correctness, not API or documentation.

verdict.wrong_value: Scalar Timedelta multiplication/division that overflows int64 (e.g. pd.Timedelta(2**62, unit='ns') * 4, * 4.5, * np.inf, or pd.Timedelta(np.iinfo(np.int64).max, unit) / 1e-30 or // 0.5) failed the internal cast without raising OutOfBoundsTimedelta, unlike vectorized TimedeltaIndex/timedelta64 Series which already raised it.
verdict.rationale: The PR fixes an out-of-bounds cast in Timedelta scalar mul/div: results exceeding int64 bounds (or non-finite float factors) should raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta with operation-specific overflow messages, matching vectorized behavior. Tests assert overflow handling, so this is an integer/float overflow defect.

verdict.wrong_value: Dividing a Timedelta scalar by a float ndarray whose quotient exceeds the int64 timedelta64[ns] range did not raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta ("Overflow in timedelta division"); the out-of-range quotient was silently computed instead of reported as overflow.
verdict.rationale: The fix adds _check_div_float_array to Timedelta.__truediv__/__floordiv__ for float ndarray divisors, invoking the OutOfBoundsTimedelta check the TimedeltaIndex path already used. An unguarded int64 timedelta64[ns] quotient outside int64 range is an overflow/invariant violation yielding a wrong result; representing quotients, zero/nan -> NaT stay unchanged. The exact wrapped value isn't recorded, so confidence is moderate.
